sentences.text: The single known specimen is an adult that preserves a complete skull, ten neck vertebrae, and a damaged left shoulder girdle.
Estimates suggest this predator measured two meters in length and weighed fifteen kilograms.
Found in 1996, the fossil was first mistaken for a Velociraptor until a CAT-scan in May 1998 proved it belonged to a new genus.
The species was formally named in December 2006 by a team including Mark Norell, James Clark, and Alan Turner.
The taxon is classified as a member of the group Dromaeosauridae.
An original analysis indicated it was a member of the subfamily Velociraptorinae.
Later studies suggested a close relationship with Linheraptor, leading some researchers to argue that Linheraptor exquisitus is a junior synonym of Tsaagan mangas.
This animal lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Campanian stage about seventy-five million years ago, in what is now Asia.
Its time range is estimated to span from eighty-three point six to seventy-two point two million years ago.
Tsaagan represents the only known dromaeosaurid remains from the Ukhaa Tolgod region aside from isolated teeth.
Xu, Pittman et al. (2015) reject the synonymy of Linheraptor exquisitus with Tsaagan mangas, citing new and existing anatomical details.
